02 / Career roadmap

My 4-year Digital VLSI journey.

A semester-wise plan from engineering fundamentals to internship and job preparation. Adapt course choices to your official university curriculum.

Year 1 — Build the foundationSemesters 1–2

Goal: become confident in mathematics, programming and digital electronics.

Semester 1 · Fundamentals

• Engineering mathematics and physics
• Basic electrical and electronic circuits
• C / Python programming
• Engineering labs and problem solving
• Linux and Git basics

Semester 2 · Digital foundations

• Number systems and Boolean algebra
• Logic gates, K-maps and minimization
• Combinational and sequential circuits
• Flip-flops, counters and registers
• Introduction to Verilog HDL
• Mini-project: digital logic design

Milestone: understand digital circuits and write simple Verilog modules.
Year 2 — Enter digital designSemesters 3–4

Goal: learn RTL design and implement circuits on FPGA.

Semester 3 · RTL design

• Digital system design
• Verilog modules, operators and data types
• Combinational and sequential RTL
• FSM design and testbenches
• Simulation with Icarus Verilog / GTKWave

Semester 4 · FPGA implementation

• Advanced Verilog and RTL coding
• FPGA architecture and constraints
• AMD Vivado design flow
• Synthesis, implementation and timing reports
• FPGA project: UART / traffic-light controller
• Start SystemVerilog fundamentals

Milestone: implement and demonstrate a working FPGA project.
Year 3 — Become industry-readySemesters 5–6

Goal: specialize in ASIC RTL design or design verification.

Semester 5 · Verification & architecture

• SystemVerilog in depth
• Computer architecture and pipelining
• Assertions and functional coverage
• Verification methodology fundamentals
• Design and verify a FIFO
• Apply for VLSI internships

Semester 6 · ASIC design flow

• RTL synthesis and design constraints
• Static timing analysis (STA)
• Setup / hold time and clock concepts
• Introduction to physical design
• UVM fundamentals and testbenches
• Target a summer internship

Milestone: complete a substantial RTL or verification project and prepare for internship interviews.
Year 4 — Specialize & launchSemesters 7–8

Goal: prove your skills through a capstone, internship and interview preparation.

Semester 7 · Advanced specialization

• Advanced RTL design and verification
• UVM project or synthesis-to-layout flow
• Low-power design concepts
• Clock-domain crossing (CDC)
• Advanced STA and debugging
• Major capstone project
• Apply to semiconductor companies

Semester 8 · Placement & growth

• Complete and document capstone
• Internship / industrial training
• Revise Verilog and SystemVerilog
• Practice RTL and verification interviews
• Prepare resume, GitHub and LinkedIn
• Apply for graduate engineer roles

Milestone: graduate with demonstrable skills, strong projects and a clear Digital VLSI career direction.
Note: This is a recommended career roadmap, not the official LPU semester syllabus. Confirm subjects, electives and prerequisites against your current programme structure.
03 / Certifications

Credentials with practical value.

Prioritize hands-on learning and verified credentials over collecting certificates. Course availability, fees and eligibility may change.

YEAR 1 · FOUNDATION

NPTEL / SWAYAM — Digital Circuits

Build fundamentals in Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential logic. Choose a current course with an assessment and certificate option.

YEAR 2 · FPGA

AMD — Vivado / FPGA Design Training

Learn FPGA architecture, RTL synthesis, implementation, constraints and timing analysis using the Vivado flow.

YEAR 2 · HDL

Verilog HDL — Hands-on course

Choose a structured course with coding exercises, testbenches, FSMs, simulation and a final project.

YEAR 3 · VERIFICATION

Cadence — Digital Design & Verification learning

Explore digital implementation and verification learning paths and practical EDA workflows where access is available.

YEAR 3 · ADVANCED VERIFICATION

SystemVerilog & UVM — Maven Silicon

Build skills in object-oriented testbenches, constrained-random verification, coverage and UVM fundamentals.

YEAR 3–4 · ASIC FLOW

Synopsys — Digital Design / EDA learning

Explore available resources in synthesis, timing analysis, verification and digital implementation.

Recommended order: Digital Design → Verilog HDL → AMD Vivado / FPGA → SystemVerilog → UVM → ASIC synthesis and STA. Check official provider websites for current course names, enrollment, fees and certificates before registering.

05 / Project portfolio

Projects & engineering practice.

My current embedded-systems project, alongside future digital design projects that support my VLSI journey.

CURRENT PROJECT · ARDUINO / EMBEDDED SYSTEMS

Water Pipe Leakage Detection System

Developing a prototype using Arduino and two water-flow sensors to compare inlet and outlet flow. The system is designed to detect abnormal flow differences and trigger an alert using a buzzer, LED and 16×2 LCD.

Components: Arduino Uno, 2 water-flow sensors, buzzer, LED, LCD and breadboard.

PLANNED · BEGINNER DIGITAL DESIGN

Digital Logic Calculator

Build adders, subtractors, multiplexers and logic functions using Verilog. Simulate and test each module.

PLANNED · INTERMEDIATE

UART Communication System

Design a UART transmitter and receiver with configurable baud rate and a complete testbench.

PLANNED · INTERMEDIATE

FIFO Memory Design

Implement synchronous FIFO in Verilog and verify full, empty, overflow and underflow conditions.

PLANNED · ADVANCED

RISC-V Processor

Develop a simple processor datapath and control unit. Explore instruction execution and pipelining.

PLANNED · CAPSTONE

ASIC RTL-to-GDSII Flow

Take a small digital design through synthesis, timing analysis and physical implementation using accessible EDA tools.

For each completed project, publish the source code, block diagram, simulation waveforms, test results and a clear README. Planned projects are labelled honestly and can be updated as they are completed.
